_comment: THE INSTALL SITE'S ENVIRONMENTS (#231).
WHAT THIS FILE DOES NOT DECIDE, and deliberately so:
· the HOSTNAME. A unit's public DN is DERIVED per environment by gov from `app_domain` plus
the base domain — prod is bare, every other env carries `-<env>` (svm-prj-work:
knowledge/deployment/specs/public-dn-convention.md, ratified PRJ-43 2026-07-28). Listing
hosts here would be a second copy of a derived fact, which is the two-copies-never-compared
pattern. `dn` below is what gov derives, recorded ONLY so the built page can print it.
· the CLIENT VERSION for a deploy. `gov-cicd deploy` owns per-env pins in
catalog/pins.yaml and `--promote <from> <to>` copies them env to env (build-once-promote).
INTERIM: prod is on gov.svayamtech.com, not gov.svayam.ai. The DN convention hardcodes the
apex, so a second SLD is not expressible yet — Svayamtech/910-GOV-CICD#273 requests
app_domain + base_domain, and that issue also carries the `former_domains` redirect requirement
so the eventual switch keeps old links working. Change `base` here when #273 lands.
THE REGISTRY IS THE CHANNEL — PRERELEASE DIST-TAGS ARE NOT NEEDED (2026-09-21). An earlier note
here said uat and dev could only diverge from prod once a `next` dist-tag existed. That was wrong,
and it mattered: it made the dev-first walkthrough look blocked on work nobody needed to do.
gov-work already declares `registries: {dev,uat -> npm.svayamtech.com, prod -> registry.npmjs.org}`,
and build-once-promote publishes a version to the DEV registry FIRST, moving that same version to
the public one on promotion. So the dev registry IS the dev channel: `pkg` names the version and
`registry` says where to get it. No prerelease, no second version scheme.
WHY `registry` IS ABSENT ON PROD, AND MUST STAY ABSENT. An empty registry means npm uses the
ADOPTER'S OWN default, which is the only correct answer for a released install — pinning prod at
our private registry would route every adopter through infrastructure they cannot reach. build.mjs
asserts both directions: non-prod must carry its pin, prod must carry none.
`pkg` AND `registry` ARE GENERATED, NOT HAND-TYPED (decided 2026-09-21). `gov-cicd deploy` renders
this file from the catalog before the image build: `semver` and `registries[env]` on the gov-work
unit are the source, and gov-install declares `deps: [gov-work]` so the content-sha cascade
redeploys this site whenever gov-work changes. Hand-editing a pin here reintroduces the
two-copies-never-compared pattern that the rest of this file warns about.
PROD PINS ONE gov RELEASE TAG (2026-09-17). `gov-work-1.2.3` was cut by `gov-cicd promote gov-work
--to prod` at cd1715b, the commit npm stamps on 1.2.3 — so the installer and the client it installs
are the SAME release. After each release: prod.ref and prod.pkg to the new tag and version, and
append the tag to `versioned`. 1.2.2 (built from c05aa80, no installer of its own) has no pair.
uat and dev pin the latest released client: gov publishes no prerelease dist-tag adopters should use.

uat.label: UAT — release candidate. Not the version to adopt.

dev.label: DEV — the tip of the dev branch. Expect it to be broken.
